patients.label: Case: two-year-old male Australian Shepherd-Poodle mixed-breed dog with an oral papilloma on the lower left lip

identity_evidence.quote: A two-year-old dog exhibited nearly complete regression of a papillomatous lesion
The papilloma was found in a two-year-old, healthy, fifty-five-pound, male, Australian Shepherd-Poodle mixed breed.

attribution_limitations: Lesion growth pattern: case text says exophytic, Figure 1 caption says endophytic
Diagnosis rests on clinical appearance; canine papillomavirus etiology not confirmed for this lesion
Total duration of the molecular iodine course is not stated

evidence.quote:
Figure 1
Canine oral papilloma at the time of discovery on the outer mucosa of the left lower lip (arrow).The lesion is endophytic with a verrucous or cauliflower-like surface and measures 7 mm in diameter.

Figure 2
A small remnant of the lesion is shown after three weeks of molecular iodine treatment (arrow).

Figure 3
The lesion site is shown four weeks after treatment with molecular iodine 300 parts per million (arrow). Tissue appears clinically healthy with no sign of recurrence.

Figure 4
The lesion site is shown one and a half years following treatment with molecular iodine (300 ppm), with no clinical sign of recurrence (arrow).

Figure 5
Proposed mechanism of action of molecular iodine in oral papilloma reso

limitations: Lesion was not examined histologically and had no polymerase chain reaction confirmation; diagnosis is clinical.

Total duration of the iodine course is not stated.
Single-animal report; treatment suggested by a dentist and not reviewed with a veterinarian.
